page: Microsoft Azure E20d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 160.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server includes 768 GB of local SSD storage, providing fast local read and write capabilities, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results position the E20d_v4 consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a PassMark CPU score of 19,245.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,491.0. Memory performance is a notable strength, with PassMark memory testing rating the configuration in the top 25% tier with a score of 2,791.74, supported by a cached read-only memory bandwidth of 1,037.19 GB/sec. For database operations, the system achieves 17.19 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and a PassMark database score of 7,212.1.

The E20d_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound applications. However, CPU-intensive tasks show moderate performance; for instance, LLM inference on a medium 7B model drops to a weak tier for prompt processing at 29.55 tokens per second. The inclusion of 768 GB of local SSD storage enhances its qualitative cost efficiency by eliminating the immediate need for external block storage for temporary data. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate data processing tasks.
